newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - DEC 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - DEC 4.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
The first Eurostar trains since the Channel Tunnel blaze left Waterloo today, but the first train at 0550 had only two genuine passengers on board.
ROCK PLAN TO END SOCIETIES BATTLE

The Northern Rock Building Society has put forward a proposal that building societies which convert to banks should be able to take over smaller societies on an agreed basis without having their takeover protection removed. Also suggested is the idea that any company which wants to bid for a converter should also be allowed to do so on an agreed basis.
PROFIT-TAKERS PUT THE POUND INTO REVERSE
Sterling fell back sharply against the dollar and the Deutschmark, as traders took profits after a month in which sterling rose 3 percent and 5 percent respectively against those currencies.

Alan Bond, the disgraced Australian businessman, pleaded guilty to two fraud charges relating to the siphoning of in excess of one billion Australian dollars from the Bell Resources Company to Bond Corporation.

Ronald Perelman, the corporate raider who took over Revlon in 1986, is frightening investors in the company, as its share price has fallen from 36.50 dollars to 29 dollars in a month over concern as to whether Perelman will honour 1.1bn dollars worth of zero-coupon bonds. -- For a full range of news monitoring services, phone BMC on
